annotations.description: Mulliganed a keepable 7-card hand that had 3 lands, a castable 2-drop (Benalish Honor Guard), and a powerful finisher (Syr Alin). While Gifted Aetherborn and Bloodbond Vampire need double black that's hard to produce, the white curve alone (Honor Guard T2, Syr Alin T5) is functional. Going to 6 cards is a significant cost when the hand already has a reasonable game plan.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. Play Thriving Heath T1 (choosing black), Plains + Honor Guard T2, and curve toward Syr Alin on T5. Draw steps may find black sources for the other cards.

annotations.description: Used basic landcycling on Ash Barrens despite already having two Mountains in hand and no black cards. This spent the turn's mana and prevented casting Lightning Visionary (1R) this turn, falling further behind on board development on turn 5 with no creatures in play.
annotations.actionTaken: Basic landcycled Ash Barrens, using 1 mana to search for a basic land
annotations.betterLine: Play a Mountain as land drop, then cast Lightning Visionary (1R) to start developing the board. Ash Barrens could be played next turn as a colorless land (useful for Stalking Drone's ability) or cycled later when there's spare mana.

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main phase with 4 untapped lands and multiple castable spells (Jousting Lance for 2, Eternal Thirst for 1B, Bloodbond Vampire for 2BB), wasting the entire turn's mana and failing to develop the board at all.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn without casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Bloodbond Vampire (2BB) to develop a 3/3 body that synergizes with the lifegain/Silversmote Ghoul plan. Alternatively, cast Jousting Lance (2) to leave up Last Gasp (1B) mana for interaction, or cast Eternal Thirst on Silversmote Ghoul for immediate lifelink pressure.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main phase with 4 untapped lands and multiple castable spells, ending the turn and wasting all mana. Bloodbond Vampire costs exactly {2}{B}{B} and is castable. Alternatively, Jousting Lance (2 mana) + Eternal Thirst on Silversmote Ghoul (2 mana) would create a powerful lifelink threat. Instead, nothing was played.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 4 mana unspent and multiple playable cards in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Bloodbond Vampire for {2}{B}{B} to develop the board. Alternatively, cast Jousting Lance ({2}) and Eternal Thirst on Silversmote Ghoul ({1}{B}) for a 5/1 lifelink creature with first strike on attacks.

annotations.description: Titan's Presence requires revealing a colorless creature with power >= the target's power. The only colorless creature in hand is Stalking Drone (power 2), but Silversmote Ghoul has power 3. The exile condition (3 ≤ 2) fails, so this spell wastes 3 mana and accomplishes nothing. Lightning Bolt was available for 1 mana and would have killed the 3/1 Ghoul.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Titan's Presence revealing Stalking Drone (power 2) targeting Silversmote Ghoul (power 3), which fails the power check and does nothing.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Bolt targeting Silversmote Ghoul to kill it for 1 mana, preserving the remaining 4 mana for deploying creatures in the second main phase (e.g., Stalking Drone + Lightning Visionary).

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main with 2 untapped Swamps and multiple strong 2-mana plays available. Eternal Thirst on Silversmote Ghoul would grant lifelink (enabling 3-life gain on attack, synergizing with Silversmote's recursion and Blood Artist). Last Gasp could remove a summoning-sick threat. Jousting Lance could be deployed. Additionally, a land drop was still available.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything or playing a land.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Eternal Thirst on Silversmote Ghoul to give it lifelink, creating a powerful synergy engine with Blood Artist and Silversmote's graveyard recursion. Alternatively, cast Last Gasp on Lightning Visionary to remove a prowess threat (triggering Blood Artist).

annotations.description: Double-blocking Silversmote Ghoul with both creatures is strictly worse than single-blocking. The Ghoul (3/1) can assign lethal damage to both the Lightning Visionary (1 toughness) and Stalking Drone (2 toughness) with its 3 power, killing all three creatures. With Blood Artist on the opponent's side, this causes 3 triggers (3 life lost, opponent gains 3) instead of 2 triggers from a single block. Libby unnecessarily loses an extra creature and gives the opponent an extra Blood Artist trigger.
annotations.actionTaken: Double-blocked Silversmote Ghoul with both Stalking Drone and Lightning Visionary
annotations.betterLine: Single-block with Stalking Drone (2/2 trades with 3/1 Ghoul, keeping Lightning Visionary alive) for only 2 Blood Artist triggers instead of 3, preserving a creature for future turns.

annotations.description: By passing without casting Last Gasp on one of the blockers, Gem31P Tactic missed the opportunity to kill both blocking creatures instead of just one. Silversmote Ghoul dies either way (1 toughness vs 4 combined damage), but casting Last Gasp on either blocker before damage would kill it, then Silversmote Ghoul's 3 damage kills the remaining blocker. This also generates an extra Blood Artist trigger. Instead, one blocker survives combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat damage step, allowing one blocker to survive.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Last Gasp on Stalking Drone (or Lightning Visionary) to kill it before combat damage, ensuring Silversmote Ghoul's 3 damage kills the remaining blocker, netting an additional creature kill and an extra Blood Artist trigger.

annotations.description: In combat, Tactic's attacking creature is blocked by Stalking Drone 2/2. The opponent has no untapped lands to activate Stalking Drone's pump ability. Casting Last Gasp on Stalking Drone would kill it before combat damage, saving Tactic's attacker and letting it deal damage through, while also triggering Blood Artist. Instead, Tactic passed, likely resulting in a trade or the attacker dying.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing combat damage to resolve normally with the block in place.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Last Gasp targeting Stalking Drone to kill it before combat damage, saving the attacking creature and pushing through damage while triggering Blood Artist.

annotations.description: Using Last Gasp during combat when Blood Artist could chump block Stalking Drone instead. Blood Artist is a 0/1 that just entered (summoning sick), but its ongoing 'whenever a creature dies' trigger provides significant value over multiple turns. However, Last Gasp is premium removal that could be saved for a bigger threat. At 22 life, the damage from Stalking Drone isn't critical, and blocking with Blood Artist + saving Last Gasp for a more impactful target (like a future Lightning Shrieker or larger creature) could be better resource management.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Last Gasp (likely targeting Stalking Drone) during blockers step, spending removal on a 2/2.
annotations.betterLine: Block Stalking Drone with Blood Artist (chump block, Blood Artist dies but triggers its own ability for 1 life drain), take 5 from Lightning Shrieker, and save Last Gasp for a higher-value target. Blood Artist's death trigger still fires, and the premium removal spell is preserved.

annotations.description: By casting Unnatural Aggression before Weaver of Lightning, Libby missed the opportunity to kill Blood Artist for free. Weaver of Lightning deals 1 damage to a target creature an opponent controls whenever you cast an instant or sorcery. Casting Weaver first (2R), then Unnatural Aggression (2G) for exactly 6 mana would have triggered Weaver to kill Blood Artist (0/1), then Stalking Drone fights and exiles Silversmote Ghoul. Instead, Libby traded away their only creature while leaving Blood Artist alive to continue draining life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Unnatural Aggression first, trading Stalking Drone for Silversmote Ghoul while Blood Artist remains on board.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Weaver of Lightning first (2R), then cast Unnatural Aggression (2G). Weaver's trigger kills Blood Artist (0/1), Stalking Drone fights and exiles Silversmote Ghoul, and Libby keeps Weaver of Lightning as a 1/4 body on board.

annotations.description: Casting Eternal Thirst on a 0/1 Blood Artist is low-value: lifelink on a 0/1 body is nearly useless since it rarely deals combat damage, and enchanting a fragile 0/1 risks a 2-for-1 if removed. The +1/+1 counter ability when opponent's creatures die has some synergy with Blood Artist's drain, but the opponent currently has no creatures on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Eternal Thirst on Blood Artist (0/1)
annotations.betterLine: Hold up Last Gasp as instant-speed removal for whatever the opponent plays next turn, or save both spells. Eternal Thirst would be much better on a larger creature like Balan later when there's more mana available.

annotations.description: Casting Last Gasp instead of Danitha Capashen, Paragon. Last Gasp kills a summoning-sick Scion Summoner (or token) for Blood Artist value, but it prevents casting Danitha this turn. Danitha (2/2 first strike, vigilance, lifelink) would start providing life gain, enable cheaper equipment costs, and is a strong board development play. The removed creature was summoning sick and not an immediate threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Last Gasp to remove a summoning-sick creature
annotations.betterLine: Cast Danitha Capashen, Paragon for 3 mana, developing a lifelink first-striker that enables cheaper Shining Armor and future equipment plays, while keeping Last Gasp as removal for a more threatening target later.

annotations.description: Failed to block Blood Artist 0/1 with any available creature. Blood Artist is a dangerous engine that triggers on every creature death. Any blocker (Scion Summoner 2/2 or Eldrazi Scion Token 1/1) would have killed the 0/1 Blood Artist while surviving themselves, removing this critical threat at the cost of only one Blood Artist death trigger (1 life loss). Instead, Blood Artist survives to continue generating value from future creature deaths.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not assign any blockers, letting Blood Artist 0/1 through.
annotations.betterLine: Block Blood Artist with Eldrazi Scion Token 1/1 (or Scion Summoner 2/2). The blocker survives since Blood Artist has 0 power, and Blood Artist dies. You take 1 life from Blood Artist's death trigger but permanently remove the engine.

annotations.description: Tactic passed priority in the precombat main phase with no creatures on board, facing multiple opposing creatures, while having Kwende castable for exactly 4 mana. Kwende is a key piece enabling the knight synergy package in hand (gives double strike to first strikers like Balan and Danitha). With no land in hand to play, there's no reason to delay. Passing here wastes the entire turn of development.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything, effectively ending the turn with no board presence.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kwende, Pride of Femeref for {3}{W} to establish a blocker and set up the knight synergy engine. Kwende's double strike ability would supercharge future plays of Balan or Danitha with Jousting Lance equipped.

annotations.description: Tactic has zero creatures on board facing multiple opposing creatures and passed their postcombat main phase without casting anything, despite having 4 mana available and Kwende (3W) as a legal cast. With Jousting Lance already on the battlefield, Kwende would effectively be a 2/2 double striker on their turn. They need board presence desperately and have a strong knight synergy hand that needs to start deploying.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main with no creatures on board, ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kwende, Pride of Femeref for 3W to start building board presence. Kwende synergizes with Jousting Lance (giving it first strike → double strike) and enables future plays like Shining Armor, Danitha, Balan, and The Circle of Loyalty.

annotations.description: At 5 life facing an opponent with Lightning Phoenix and multiple creatures, Danitha Capashen, Paragon would have been the better play. Danitha's lifelink is critical for stabilizing at low life, and her first strike + vigilance make her a superior blocker. She also costs 1 less mana (leaving more open for future plays) and reduces Equipment spell costs. Kwende's double strike granting ability has no targets yet since no other first strikers are on the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kwende, Pride of Femeref (3W) - a 2/2 double strike with no other first strikers to buff
annotations.betterLine: Cast Danitha Capashen, Paragon (2W) for a 2/2 first strike, vigilance, lifelink that stabilizes life total and enables future synergies with Kwende and equipment

annotations.description: Kwende blocks Lightning Phoenix, which will return from the graveyard at end of turn since the opponent dealt 4 damage to Tactic this combat (satisfying the 3+ damage condition). Blocking Scion Summoner instead would also result in exactly 4 unblocked damage (surviving at 1 life) but would permanently remove a 2/2 creature rather than trading for one that comes right back.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Lightning Phoenix with Kwende, Pride of Femeref
annotations.betterLine: Block Scion Summoner with Kwende to permanently remove a 2/2 threat, since Lightning Phoenix will return from the graveyard anyway when the 4 unblocked combat damage satisfies its trigger condition.
